pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔤 **Strand 2 — Algebra**
Using letters and symbols to describe patterns, relationships and unknown quantities.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B8.2.1)
- B8.2.1.1 — Demonstrate the ability to draw tables of values for a linear relation, graph the relation in a number plane, determine the gradient of the line and use it to write the equation of a line of the form y = mx + c.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- explain gradient as steepness using real-life examples
- find the gradient from two points, from an equation and from a graph
- write the equation of a line in slope-intercept form (y = mx + c) and point-slope form
- use graphs of linear relations to find missing values and solve real-life problems

lessons.title: The gradient of a line

pages.title: The gradient of a line
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Calculate the gradient of a line and use it to write the equation of a line in the form y = mx + c.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.1.1.1
## Gradient in real life
The **gradient** (slope) of a line measures how **steep** it is. A cyclist climbing a hill feels the gradient of the road; a carpenter sets the gradient (pitch) of a roof so that rain water runs off.
[[fig:m8-f12|Figure 5.1: Gradient of a hill and of a roof]]
> 🔑 **Key idea: Gradient** — Gradient = [[rise/run]] = [[change in y/change in x]]. For a line through (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂): **m =** [[y_{2} − y_{1}/x_{2} − x_{1}]]. A line rising from left to right has a **positive** gradient; falling has a **negative** gradient; horizontal has gradient **0**; vertical lines have no defined gradient.
[[fig:m8-f13|Figure 5.2: Positive, negative and zero gradients]]
## ✏️ Example 5.1
Find the gradient of the line through: a) A(1, 1) and B(7, 2) b) P(−2, 4) and Q(3, 5) c) C(3, −2) and D(−3, 4)
**Solution**
a) m = [[2 − 1/7 − 1]] = [[1/6]]
b) m = [[5 − 4/3 − (−2)]] = [[1/5]]
c) m = [[4 − (−2)/−3 − 3]] = [[6/−6]] = **−1**
## Gradient from an equation
When the equation is written as **y = mx + c**, the coefficient of x (**m**) is the gradient and **c** is the **y-intercept** (where the line crosses the y-axis).
## ✏️ Example 5.2
Find the gradient of: a) y = 5x + 13 b) 2x − 8y + 3 = 0 c) y = −3x + 12
**Solution**
a) **m = 5**
b) Make y the subject: 8y = 2x + 3 ⟹ y = [[1/4]]x + [[3/8]], so **m =** [[1/4]]
c) **m = −3**

pages.title: Example 5.3
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 5.3
Determine the gradient of the line in the graph.
[[fig:m8-f14]]
Figure 5.3: Line through A(−8, −2) and B(2, 3)
**Solution**
From the graph, A(−8, −2) and B(2, 3) lie on the line.
m = [[3 − (−2)/2 − (−8)]] = [[5/10]] = [[1/2]]
## Equation of a line
> 🔑 **Key idea: Forms of the equation of a line** — **Slope-intercept form:** y = mx + c (gradient m, y-intercept c). **Point-slope form:** y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) (gradient m, through the point (x₁, y₁)).
## ✏️ Example 5.4
a) Find the equation of the line with gradient 2 and y-intercept −3. Hence find y when x = 4. b) Find the equation of the line with y-intercept 7 and gradient −2. c) Find the equation of the line with gradient [[2/3]] and y-intercept 4.
**Solution**
a) **y = 2x − 3**. When x = 4: y = 8 − 3 = **5**.
b) **y = −2x + 7**
c) **y =** [[2/3]]**x + 4** (or 3y = 2x + 12)
## ✏️ Example 5.5
a) Find the equation of the line with gradient 2 through (3, 5). b) Find the equation of the line through (3, −7) with gradient [[1/2]]. c) Find the equation of the line through (5, 4) and (−1, −2). d) Write 5x + 4y − 3 = 0 in the form y = mx + c and state the gradient and intercept.
**Solution**
a) y − 5 = 2(x − 3) ⟹ y = 2x − 6 + 5 ⟹ **y = 2x − 1**
b) y + 7 = [[1/2]](x − 3) ⟹ 2y + 14 = x − 3 ⟹ **2y = x − 17** (y = [[1/2]]x − [[17/2]])
c) m = [[−2 − 4/−1 − 5]] = [[−6/−6]] = 1; y − 4 = 1(x − 5) ⟹ **y = x − 1**
d) 4y = −5x + 3 ⟹ **y = −**[[5/4]]**x +** [[3/4]]; gradient **−**[[5/4]], y-intercept [[3/4]]

pages.title: Exercise 5.1
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 5.1** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Find the gradient of the line through: a) (2, 3) and (6, 11) b) (−1, 5) and (3, −3) c) (0, −4) and (5, −4) d) (−3, −2) and (1, 6)
2. State the gradient and y-intercept: a) y = 4x − 7 b) y = −x + 2 c) 3y = 6x + 9 d) 2x + 5y = 10
3. Find the equation of the line: a) gradient 3, y-intercept −2 b) gradient −[[1/2]], through (4, 1) c) through (1, 2) and (3, 8) d) through (−2, 5) and (4, −1)
4. A road rises 15 m over a horizontal distance of 300 m. Find its gradient as a fraction and a percentage.
5. Show that the points (1, 3), (3, 7) and (6, 13) lie on the same straight line.

parts.a: Each pair has gradient 2 (and all satisfy y = 2x + 1).

pages.title: Using graphs to find missing values
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use the graph of a linear relation to determine subsequent missing elements in the ordered pairs of the relation.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.1.1.2
## ✏️ Example 5.6
The graph represents y = 20x, where y is the cost (GH₵) and x is the weight (kg) of meat sold at a market.
[[fig:m8-f15]]
Figure 5.4: Cost of meat: y = 20x
Use the graph to find: a) the cost of 3.5 kg of meat b) the weight of meat that can be bought with GH₵80 c) Using the relation, how many kilograms can be bought for GH₵240?
**Solution**
a) Read up from x = 3.5 to the line, then across: **GH₵70**
b) Read across from y = 80 to the line, then down: **4 kg**
c) 20x = 240 ⟹ **x = 12 kg** (beyond the graph, so use the equation)
## ✏️ Example 5.7
The diameter of a wawa tree is 10 inches. It grows at an average rate of [[1/2]] inch per year, so y = [[1/2]]x + 10 gives its diameter y (inches) after x years. a) Complete the table. b) What will the diameter be after 40 years?
**Solution**
a)
| **x (years)** | **0** | **10** | **20** | **30** | **50** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y (inches) | 10 | 15 | 20 | 25 | 35 |
[[fig:m8-f16]]
Figure 5.5: Diameter of a wawa tree
b) y = [[1/2]] × 40 + 10 = **30 inches**

pages.title: Using linear graphs to solve real-life problems
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use graphs of linear relations to solve real-life problems.
Curriculum indicator B8.2.1.1.3
## ✏️ Example 5.8
Every morning you go for a walk. The distance walked can be modelled by d = 4h, where d is in kilometres and h is the number of hours. Make a table, draw the graph and find how far you walk in 6 hours.
**Solution**
| **Time h (hours)** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** | **6** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Distance d (km) | 4 | 8 | 12 | 16 | 20 | 24 |
[[fig:m8-f17]]
Figure 5.6: Distance walked: d = 4h
After 6 hours you walk **24 km**. The gradient, 4, is the walking speed (4 km/h).
## ✏️ Example 5.9
Nhyira paints portraits. The graph shows how much she charges based on the time taken.
[[fig:m8-f18]]
Figure 5.7: Nhyira's charges
a) How much does she charge for a portrait that takes 3 hours? b) If she charges GH₵175, how many hours did she spend? c) How many hours for a portrait costing GH₵300? d) Write the equation of the line and explain what the y-intercept means.
**Solution**
a) **GH₵175** b) **3 hours** (the same point) c) From the line (or equation): 50h + 25 = 300 ⟹ **h = 5.5 hours**
d) The line passes through (0, 25) and (2, 125): gradient = [[100/2]] = 50. **Cost = 50h + 25**. The intercept GH₵25 is a fixed charge (e.g. for materials) before any painting time; GH₵50 is charged per hour.

pages.title: Exercise 5.3
pages.body:

1. A plumber charges GH₵60 for a call-out plus GH₵40 per hour. Write an equation for the cost C after h hours, draw its graph for 0 ≤ h ≤ 6 and use it to find the cost of a 3.5-hour job and the time spent on a job costing GH₵260.
2. A tank holds 500 litres and is being emptied at 25 litres per minute. Write an equation for the volume V after t minutes. When will the tank be empty? What does the gradient represent?

A tank holds 500 litres and is being emptied at 25 litres per minute. Write an equation for the volume V after t minutes. When will the tank be empty? What does the gradient represent?

parts.a: V = 500 − 25t; after 20 minutes; the gradient −25 is the rate of emptying (25 litres per minute)

pages.title: Chapter 5 summary
pages.body:
- Gradient m = [[y_{2} − y_{1}/x_{2} − x_{1}]] = rise ÷ run.
- y = mx + c: m is the gradient, c is the y-intercept. Point-slope form: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
- Read values from a linear graph by going up/across to the line; use the equation for values outside the graph.
- In real-life graphs, the gradient is a rate and the intercept is a starting (fixed) value.
